examples.en: Gyeongju was the capital of Silla.
The capital of Joseon is today's Seoul.

examples.ko: 왕은 새로운 도읍지를 찾으려고 신하들을 보냈어요.
examples.en: The king sent his officials to find a new capital.

examples.ko: 이 유적은 옛 백제의 도읍지에 있어요.
examples.en: These ruins are in the old capital of Baekje.
As the capital changed, the look of the city changed too.
I took a trip to Buyeo, which is famous as a former capital.

explain: 옛 나라의 수도를 말할 때 쓰고, 역사 이야기에서 자주 만나요. 지금의 나라 수도는 보통 '수도'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The capital of Silla was Gyeongju.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻이고 일상에서 더 널리 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, and the more widely used word in daily life.

phrases.en: King Taejo chose Hanyang as the capital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 역사 이야기에서 수도를 정하는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in history stories when a capital is chosen.

phrases.en: Buyeo is a former capital of Baekje.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금은 수도가 아닌 옛 수도를 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a former capital that is no longer the capital.

explain_en: It refers to the capital of an old kingdom and shows up in talk about history. For the capital of a country today, people usually say '수도'.

examples.ko: 이 섬의 북단에는 등대가 하나 서 있어요.
examples.en: There is a lighthouse at the northern end of this island.
The typhoon moved up all the way to the northern end of the Korean Peninsula.

examples.ko: 호수 북단에서 해가 지는 모습을 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched the sun set from the northern end of the lake.

examples.ko: 열차는 도시의 북단에 있는 역에서 출발해요.
examples.en: The train departs from the station at the northern edge of the city.

examples.ko: 반도 북단으로 갈수록 날씨가 더 추워져요.
examples.en: The closer you get to the northern end of the peninsula, the colder it gets.
I pointed at the northern area on the map with my finger.

explain: 어떤 지역에서 가장 북쪽 끝부분을 가리켜요. 반대로 남쪽 끝은 '남단'이라고 하고, 일상 대화에서는 '북쪽 끝'이라고 더 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: We visited the northernmost village in the country.
phrases.nuance_ko: '최'를 붙이면 가장 북쪽 끝이라는 뜻이 더 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '최' makes it clearer that it is the very northern end.

phrases.en: That city is at the northern end of the island.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위치를 설명할 때 조사 '에'와 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with the particle '에' to describe a location.
phrases.en_equiv: to be at the northern end

phrases.example: 이 길은 마을 북쪽 끝까지 이어져요.
phrases.en: This road continues to the northern end of the village.
phrases.nuance_ko: '북단'의 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The everyday way to say '북단'.

explain_en: It points to the very northern edge of a region. The opposite, the southern end, is '남단', and in everyday conversation people more often say '북쪽 끝'.

examples.en: A divider is installed in the middle of the road.
The car crashed into the divider.

examples.ko: 분리대 때문에 반대편으로 바로 건너갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: Because of the divider, you can't cross straight to the other side.

examples.ko: 자전거 도로와 차도 사이에 분리대를 세웠어요.
examples.en: They put up a barrier between the bike path and the road.
The barrier in front of the construction site has fallen over.
I can see the opposite lane over the divider.

explain: 차선이나 길을 나누려고 세운 구조물이에요. 도로 한가운데 있는 건 '중앙분리대'라고 하는 경우가 많아요. 뉴스에서 교통사고 이야기를 할 때도 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The car hit the median barrier.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도로 한가운데 있는 분리대를 가리키는 가장 흔한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common term for a barrier in the middle of a road.

phrases.en: The city installed a barrier on the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공사나 안전 대책을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about construction or safety measures.

phrases.en: I almost hit the barrier while driving on a night road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교통사고 이야기에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing in talk about traffic accidents.

explain_en: It is a structure built to separate lanes or paths. The one in the very middle of a road is often called '중앙분리대'. It also comes up often in news about traffic accidents.

examples.ko: 이민자들은 새 정착지를 찾아 먼 길을 떠났어요.
examples.en: The immigrants set off on a long journey to find a new place to settle.
This village used to be a settlement of nomads.
As soon as we arrived at our new home town, we looked for a house first.
The refugees spent the winter in a temporary settlement.

examples.ko: 우리 가족의 마지막 정착지는 제주도가 될 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think Jeju Island will be our family's final place to settle.

examples.ko: 정착지를 정할 때는 일자리와 학교가 중요해요.
examples.en: When choosing where to settle, jobs and schools are important.

explain: 여기저기 옮겨 다니다가 자리를 잡고 살게 된 곳을 말할 때 써요. '거주지'는 지금 살고 있는 곳을 가리키는 딱딱한 말이라 느낌이 조금 달라요. 이민, 이주, 역사 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 이 섬이 그들의 최종 정착지가 되었어요.
phrases.en: This island became their final settlement.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 곳을 옮겨 다닌 끝에 자리 잡은 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the place where people finally settled after moving around.

phrases.en: This village became a settlement for immigrants.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 곳이 사람들이 자리 잡는 곳으로 바뀔 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a place becomes somewhere people settle.

phrases.example: 그는 외국에서 오랫동안 떠돌다가 이 도시에 정착했어요.
phrases.en: After wandering abroad for a long time, he settled in this city.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정착지와 짝이 되는 동사로, 사람이 주어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb that pairs with 정착지; the subject is a person.

explain_en: It is used for a place where people finally settled down after moving around. '거주지' (residence) is a more formal word for where you live now, so the feel is a bit different. It often appears in talk about immigration, migration and history.

examples.en: The medical staff worked on the front line fighting the infectious disease.

examples.ko: 소방관들은 재난 현장의 최전선에 서 있어요.
examples.en: Firefighters stand on the front line of disaster sites.
The cutting edge of research is always busy and hard.

examples.ko: 그 기자는 전쟁 최전선으로 취재를 갔어요.
examples.en: The reporter went to the war's front line to cover it.

examples.ko: 시장 최전선을 지키는 사람은 바로 판매 직원이에요.
examples.en: The ones who guard the market's front line are the sales staff.

examples.ko: 고객을 만나는 최전선이 바로 이 매장이에요.
examples.en: This store is the front line where we meet customers.

explain: 전쟁에서 적과 가장 가까운 맨 앞쪽을 뜻하고, 비유로 어떤 일에서 가장 앞에서 부딪치는 현장을 말하기도 해요. 비슷한 말은 '일선'이고, 반대는 '후방'이에요. 뉴스에서 의료, 소방, 연구 이야기에 자주 비유로 나와요.

phrases.en: Firefighters work at the forefront, fighting the flames.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에서'를 붙여 어떤 일이 벌어지는 가장 앞쪽 현장을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '에서' it marks the place at the very front where the work happens.

phrases.example: 그분은 오랫동안 교육 일선에서 아이들을 가르쳤어요.
phrases.en: He taught children on the front line of education for many years.
phrases.nuance_ko: '최전선'과 비슷하지만 전쟁 느낌이 덜하고 일하는 현장을 가리킬 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '최전선' but with less of a war feel; it is used more for the front line of ordinary work.

phrases.example: 연구자들은 새로운 기술의 최전선에 서 있어요.
phrases.en: Researchers stand at the forefront of new technology.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 분야에서 가장 앞서서 일하는 사람을 비유로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively for people leading the way in a field.

explain_en: It means the very front closest to the enemy in a war, and figuratively the place at the very front of any field where people face things first. A similar word is '일선', and the opposite is '후방' (rear). In the news it often appears figuratively about medicine, firefighting and research.

examples.en: Please enter the departure point and the destination.
The flight departs from Incheon.
It takes two hours from the starting point to the destination.
I entered the wrong departure point in the taxi app.
Let's meet near the starting point and go together.
The departure point is Seoul and the destination is Busan.

explain: 반대말은 '도착지'예요. 내비게이션, 택시 앱, 여행 계획에서 자주 봐요. '출발점'은 시작하는 지점이나 시작 자체를 말할 때도 써서 조금 더 넓어요.

phrases.en: Please check the departure and arrival points.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말과 함께 자주 붙여 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly paired with its opposite.

phrases.en: I chose Seoul Station as the starting point of the trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어디에서 떠날지 결정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when deciding where to set off from.

phrases.en: This is the starting point of the walking trail.
phrases.nuance_ko: 출발지보다 넓게, 시작하는 지점을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Broader than 출발지; any starting point.

explain_en: The opposite is '도착지'. You often see it in navigation, taxi apps and travel plans. '출발점' is broader, as it can also mean the beginning of something.

examples.ko: 길가에 공사 중이라는 푯말이 서 있어요.
examples.en: A sign saying 'under construction' stands by the road.
I followed the signpost and took the right road.
They put up a sign telling people to keep off the grass.

examples.ko: 푯말에 적힌 글씨가 흐려서 안 보여요.
examples.en: The writing on the sign is faded and I can't read it.

examples.ko: 등산로마다 푯말이 있어서 길을 잃지 않아요.
examples.en: Every hiking trail has signposts, so you don't get lost.

examples.ko: 밭 입구에 주인 이름을 적은 푯말도 있어요.
examples.en: There is also a sign with the owner's name at the field entrance.

explain: '표지판'과 비슷한데, 푯말은 말뚝이나 나무판에 글씨를 써서 세워 둔 작은 것을 떠올리게 해요. 도로나 건물의 공식 안내판은 '표지판'이 더 자연스러워요. '푯말을 세우다, 푯말이 서 있다'로 자주 써요.

phrases.en: A new road sign has been put up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 푯말보다 공식적이고 큰 안내판에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for larger, official signs rather than small posts.

phrases.en: They put up a signpost at the park entrance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 설치할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used when installing a new one.

phrases.en: The sign says 'No entry'.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글자 내용을 알려 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to tell what is written on it.
phrases.en_equiv: to be written on the sign

explain_en: It is close to '표지판', but '푯말' suggests a small sign written on a stake or wooden board. For official road or building signs, '표지판' sounds more natural. It commonly goes with '푯말을 세우다' and '푯말이 서 있다'.
